description: Named stress scenarios for the fictional demo business in demo_business.json. SYNTHETIC / ILLUSTRATIVE: invented deterministic stress paths chosen to exercise MATH_MODEL §1, not forecasts and not based on any real company or real event.

scenarios.name: Rate shock: +200bp from week 1
scenarios.rationale: The term loan floats, so a 2-point rise in the base rate passes straight into interest: 600,000 x 2% / 52 = 230.77 more per week.

scenarios.name: Demand drop: -20% for 6 weeks, 4-week recovery
scenarios.rationale: A local slowdown cuts footfall by a fifth for six weeks, then customers return gradually; lost sales cost the 35% gross margin while purchases fall with them.

scenarios.name: Supplier outage: primary distributor down for 3 weeks
scenarios.rationale: The primary distributor cannot deliver in weeks 5-7, so the 40% of base-store sales on its product lines are lost unless the backup supplier is used.

shock.name: Supplier outage: primary distributor down for 3 weeks

scenarios.name: Bad quarter: rate shock + demand drop + supplier outage
scenarios.rationale: All three shocks above hit in the same quarter, so higher interest, weaker footfall and a supply gap compound on a business that already loses about 1,400 a week.

shock.name: Bad quarter: rate shock + demand drop + supplier outage
